Comment: SurgiSync web production - SPA from S3 + /api and /health proxied to the production ALB
_comment: PriceClass_100 (NA + EU) rather than staging's PriceClass_All. A deliberate divergence, not drift - there is no known user base outside NA/EU and the cheaper class is the correct default until there is. Revisit by changing this one field; it needs no recreate.

Items._comment: MUST be www.surgisoftsolutions.com. It is the only value that both passes origin TLS validation (it is the exact subject of the ALB's default listener certificate, the www-only 8d1d34e4-...) and produces a Host matching the ALB's priority-3 host-header rule. READ THIS BEFORE COPYING FROM cloudfront-staging.json: the staging file warns that a non-matching Host falls to the ALB default rule and silently reaches PRODUCTION. Here that warning inverts and stops being a guard, because the default rule forwards to hoosier-tg-v1-prod, which is where this distribution wants to be - so a wrong value fails silently AND looks correct. The one wrong value that matters is leaving staging.surgisoftsolutions.com in place, which puts production users on the STAGING database while every other check on this distribution still passes. /health/data/ returning "env": "production" is the only cheap detector. Do not simplify to the raw ALB hostname: the wildcard certificate does not cover it and origin TLS fails with a 502. Do not add www.surgisoftsolutions.com to Aliases on this distribution - that is a loop.

DefaultCacheBehavior._comment: AWS managed SecurityHeadersPolicy. It sends exactly five headers - X-XSS-Protection, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Strict-Transport-Security - and NO Content-Security-Policy. That absence is load-bearing for Kit Detail's Live Location map, which fetches its basemap cross-origin. A CSP without maps.googleapis.com in img-src leaves the map an empty grey box in production while it renders perfectly in dev, because nothing else in the app loads a third-party asset. Add tile.openstreetmap.org too only if a deployed build is ever meant to fall back to Leaflet on OSM (VITE_MAP_TILE_URL); that path also needs style-src-attr, because Leaflet sets inline style attributes on its tiles and panes, while the Google path is a single and needs neither. The Referrer-Policy above is separately load-bearing for Google: the Static Maps key is restricted by HTTP referrer, and strict-origin-when-cross-origin is what sends the origin that restriction matches on. Weakening it to no-referrer would 403 every map with no other symptom. NOTE FOR PRODUCTION: this distribution ships whichever provider the deploy workflow had credentials for - see the tile provider tripwire in web-deploy-prod.yml, which fires on every production deploy that falls back to OpenStreetMap. A commercial provider must be settled before real users.

Items._comment: Not optional. /health/data/ is routed at hoosier/urls.py outside /api/, so without this it falls to the S3 behaviour and returns index.html with a 200 - and its "env" field is the only cheap detector for the origin trap described on the alb-prod origin above. On this distribution it must read "production"; "staging" means the origin was copied from cloudfront-staging.json and production users are reading and writing the staging database. It exposes nothing new; the endpoint is already public on www.surgisoftsolutions.com.

CustomErrorResponses._comment: TTL-0 only, and deliberately no custom error PAGE - ResponsePagePath is the empty string on every entry, which is CloudFront's way of saying there is none. CloudFront caches 4xx/5xx for 10s even under Managed-CachingDisabled, and that policy excludes the query string from the cache key, so a 503 on ?page=1 could be replayed for ?page=2. An actual response page would be worse than the caching: CustomErrorResponses is distribution-wide, so it would also turn the API's genuine 403s and 404s into a 200 serving index.html. The SPA fallback lives in the viewer-request function instead (infra/spa-router.js). 504 is included because OriginReadTimeout is 60s and gateway timeouts are reachable. Quantity must match the array length. ResponsePagePath and ResponseCode are spelled out rather than omitted: create-distribution defaults them, but update-distribution rejects a partially-specified member of this list with 'The specified list of custom error responses does not exist or is not valid' - so omitting them makes a newly added error code impossible to apply to an existing distribution.
